parsed.explanation: Combined regime is elevated risk: federal entry, passport, federal-facility and custody exposures are documented and universal, while this state has no bathroom or adult-care ban and is assessed as largely refraining from targeting adults. State protections are patchwork and do not cancel federal discretionary refusal, possible fraud ineligibility, federal facility exclusion, or documented immigration-custody abuse. Litigation and local ordinances provide only partial, uneven recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary passport regime, Supreme Court allowance, visa discretion where documents cast doubt on sex, possible permanent fraud ineligibility, reported confiscations; no state X option is resident-facing.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; passport policy under court challenge; legal-aid guidance available.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger federal refusal or fraud inquiry before any state protection applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal prison policies mandate hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State prisoner hormone right established historically, but federal policy and abuse reports show no operative remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry or facility referral into detention exposes traveller to federal custody practices regardless of state law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal government-funded single-sex facilities barred congruent with gender identity; some state bans elsewhere do not apply here.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State has no law barring bathroom/facility use consistent with identity and no sex-definition exclusion.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State buildings are comparatively open, but federal buildings, bases and federally controlled spaces remain excluded.

care_services.exposure: National funding pressure led two major hospital systems in Jan 2026 to pause pharmacologic care under 18; federal orders target minor care and school social transition.
care_services.protection: No state minor-care ban; governor vetoed bans in 2023-24; mental-health services continued; state AG joined challenge.
care_services.interaction: Adult care is not banned locally, but federal funding and enforcement pressure can reach travelling minors and families.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; executive orders direct investigations and passport/facility sex definitions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several federal orders blocked or enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; marriage and 2020 employment ruling remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises discretionary enforcement risk, while injunctions and unresolved suits create timing uncertainty.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal school investigation/prosecution directive, care funding threats and hospital pauses affect a minor traveller and guardian; state legislature repeatedly passed restrictive bills.
minors_guardians.protection: Governor vetoes kept state bans from enactment and state AG contested federal health declaration; status of challenge unresolved.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family can face federal school, health-funding and document scrutiny despite state vetoes.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide gender-identity discrimination law and gender identity absent from state hate-crime statute; prosecutors sometimes route via perceived sexual orientation, not documented as systematic.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2019 state executive order covers state employment, contracting and services; some cities fully cover employment, housing and public accommodations for 21% of population.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local ordinances help in some cities but leave most of state without full state-level recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suits, executive-order challenges and health-rule litigation unresolved; individual entry or facility remedies are slow and discretionary.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several federal measures and state AG participates in multistate litigation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved federal litigation means protection depends on measure and date of travel; not_documented for traveller-specific outcomes.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal federal exclusion and discretionary entry, but here refusal is administrative rather than routine entry bar, state facilities are open, and courts have enjoined some measures, so higher than 0.35.
Close: document divergence leads to secondary screening, hours of delay and possible discretionary refusal with slow remedies; federal fraud exposure and custody abuse make this case somewhat lower.

Higher safety than this case: 0.75 has respectful border training, brief detention and compensation; here federal binary rules, facility exclusion and custody harm are documented, so materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: State law is comparatively benign for adults, with no facility ban and vetoed minor-care restrictions, but the traveller's journey is governed also by federal border, passport, federal-facility and detention systems. Those systems create universal document exposure, discretionary refusal, and severe custody risk if detained, with only patchwork local protection and unresolved federal litigation. Families face additional federal care and school pressure despite state vetoes. The result is elevated, not severe, risk.
